data.narrative:
Mujin is a Series C robotics and manufacturing automation company that has raised $85M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), selected for sector alignment and stage proximity.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $85M total raised as a valuation proxy, applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $144M. Peer-median analysis examines seven same-sector comparables at Series B and D stages—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D)—establishing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: $123M (low), $897M (median), and $1.9B (high). The 15x spread reflects material uncertainty in how Mujin's revenue trajectory, market traction, and competitive positioning map to peer outcomes. The peer-median figure of $1.6B may overstate valuation if Mujin lags leading comparables on deployment scale or unit economics; the stage-progression figure of $144M likely understates it given sector momentum. A defensible range of $400M–$1.2B would align Mujin within peer precedent while accounting for stage and execution risk.
